_comment: Scan list for the ex-vivo micro-CT segmentation pipeline. Set 'box' to the folder holding the Ex-Vivo data (Human Eye/, Pig Eye/, the 3D Slicer markups) and 'ct' to an optional local copy of the CT slice stacks, used for speed when present (local_xdir). Paths may use {box} and {ct}. f = in-plane+slice downsampling factor for the working volume. bath: air | liquid. shell: true for collapsed/fixed eyes whose scleral shell must be closed before filling.
ct: <optional local copy of the CT stacks>

axis_ring._comment: Eye axis = normal of the holder ring plate (the eye always sits stump down through the ring, cornea up). Used for the listed groups when a plate is found plate_to_centre_mm below the globe centroid and centred within max_off_centre_mm; otherwise the lens / nerve-stump cues decide.

globe_surface._comment: method: smooth_star | opening (legacy, 3 mm opening; always used for shell eyes). Lengths in mm, angles in degrees. tol = how far a tissue edge may lie from the smooth surface and still be followed; band = how far from the stiff baseline an edge may lie and still be used; morph = half-width of the bumps/notches removed on the sphere.

mri._comment: Pig MRI, Agilent 9.4 T, sequence gems (Ex-Vivo/MRI parameters.jpg): TR 550 ms, TE 7.5 ms, flip 20 deg, 16 averages, data matrix 512 x 512 over 40 x 40 mm (0.078 mm acquired, not interpolated), 36 slices of 0.8 mm, no gap, interleaved, no fat saturation, coil 72 mm volume. The eyes were in oil: the bath is displaced by the chemical shift. Along the rows the shift is computed from the DICOM tags (1.12 mm). Across the slices it depends on the radio-frequency pulse bandwidth, which is recorded nowhere; oil_slice_shift_mm is the value measured on the five fresh eyes (one-sided empty band across the slices 1.12-1.38 mm, minus the dark wall 0-0.38 mm: median 1.0 mm), applied to all of them because they share one protocol. No such band is seen in the preserved eyes (0).
